title: Alpha and Omega (Revelation 1:1–8)
hookLine: grace and peace from the one who is, who was, and who is to come

cards: From: John. To: the seven churches which are in Asia. Before any dragon or trumpet, Revelation reads like mail: who it's from, who it's to.

Then the greeting, ordinary and not ordinary at all: "Grace be unto you, and peace, from him which is, and which was, and which is to come." These are real congregations in real cities, each with a name you'll meet soon.
And the letter opens by naming God in a strange order. Today, the first eight verses, ending at a pair of letters.

teach.h: IS, WAS, IS TO COME: NOW COMES FIRST.
teach.b: First, the order. You'd expect: who was, who is, who will be. John writes: who is, who was, who is to come.
He starts with now. Some readers hear in it the name God gives Moses at the burning bush, I AM. Before God is a memory or a hope, God is present, today.
The letter sends grace "from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth." A witness who told the truth, even to death.
The firstborn from the dead. A ruler over the rulers. For churches under pressure, that last title would land.

teach.h: A SONG: UNTO HIM THAT LOVED US.
teach.b: John can't finish his greeting without breaking into praise: "Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood." Praise breaks into the middle of the mail. Fourth, the signature.
God speaks in the first person: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty."

Alpha and omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, like saying A to Z. Every word, every story, sits between them. The claim isn't only that God was there at the start and will be at the finish.

teach.h: A TO Z: THE WHOLE ALPHABET.
teach.b: God holds the whole alphabet, including the messy middle where the seven churches were living, and where everybody lives.

how: The Greek letters alpha and omega appear on Christian altars, candles and vestments; in some churches the Easter candle is marked with them as a sign that Christ is the beginning and the end.

games.q: you're John, writing to seven churches in Asia. how do you begin?
o: with a warning of what's coming.
with grace and peace, from the one who is, and was, and is to come.
with a vision of a dragon.
games.why: he begins like a letter, with grace and peace. the dragons can wait; the first word to the churches is a greeting.

practice: Hold the first thing you did today and the last thing you expect to do tonight like bookends, and let everything in between come gently into view: the conversations, the work, the worry, the small good things.
If you pray, say quietly, I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, and rest your whole day between those letters; if not, just let the day be held, start to finish, for a moment.

wordCard.voice: Alpha and Omega. The first and last letters of the Greek alphabet, and Revelation's name for the one who holds everything from A to Z.

orig.note: Greek: the first and last letters of the alphabet. God's signature in Revelation 1:8: the beginning and the ending.

carryVoice: Your line: the beginning and the end. The week ran from the Orthodox way through Koyama, Mbiti and Polkinghorne to Revelation's opening verses. That's the week.
